title: docs(spec): `input.options` during `before*` is the caller's engine options bag, not `DriverOptions` — correct the `HookContext.input` contract table and pin it
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5997

An observation-class finding: the runtime is correct, the prose describing it is not. This PR changes prose plus one pin test. No runtime behaviour changes, the accepted set does not move.

## Premise verification (against `origin/main`, line numbers re-derived)

All three legs still hold. Both the issue's and triage's line numbers had drifted; these are the ones I measured at `b70e534cc`:

| Fact | Location |
|:--|:--|
| Both `before` rows still say `options: DriverOptions` | `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts:338` / `:341` |
| `beforeUpdate` context is built from the caller's options | `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:5792` — `input: { id, data: opCtx.data, options: opCtx.options }` |
| `beforeUpdate` fires, and only then `buildDriverOptions` | `:5800` then `:5801` |
| `beforeDelete` context, same shape | `:6350` — `input: { id, options: opCtx.options }` |
| `beforeDelete` fires, and only then `buildDriverOptions` | `:6425` then `:6440` |
| Both break-glass guards still read that slot | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts:190` (header), `:792` (comment), `:886` / `:957` (the reads) |

Probed on the real engine, the four write shapes agree with the issue's better-sqlite3 probe:

```
update by-id : input.id = 'r_1',     input.options = { where: { id: 'r_1' } }
update multi : input.id = undefined, input.options = { multi: true, where: { status: 'todo' } }
delete by-id : input.id = 'r_1',     input.options = { where: { id: 'r_1' } }
delete multi : input.id = undefined, input.options = { multi: true, where: { id: { $in: ['r_2','r_3'] } } }
```

Reference identity `input.options === callerOptions` is `true` in all four: the handler receives the caller's very object.

## One correction to the issue's own framing (measured stronger, not weaker)

The issue says the slot "becomes `DriverOptions` after the hooks return", which reads as a replacement. Measured, `buildDriverOptions` (`engine.ts:1781`) is an ADDITIVE MERGE: `const opts = base && typeof base === 'object' ? { ...base } : {}`, then only `if (... === undefined) opts.X = ...` assignments — it never deletes a key, and with no transaction / tenant / timezone / system flag it returns `base` itself unchanged. So the caller's `where` and `multi` are never stripped; the `after*` bag is simply the same bag with driver-side keys added. The prose is written to that measurement rather than to "replacement".

`packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts:543` corroborates this independently: "`input.options` is rebuilt by `buildDriverOptions` as a COPY of the caller's bag, so `multi` is still there".

## What changed

**1. `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` — the contract table.** The two `before` rows now carry the measured shape (`EngineUpdateOptions` / `EngineDeleteOptions`). The `options` cell is also marked phase-dependent and a new `PHASE` paragraph states the rule, because the phase pattern measurably holds on *every* path (`find` `:5057` then `:5058`, `insert` `:5322` then `:5332`, and both write paths). Fixing two rows while their neighbours keep saying the opposite would leave the next author tripping over the same thing.

**2. Both statements are preserved, with the difference spelled out** — the core deliverable of this card, and what two security guards depend on:

- what a hook CANNOT reach is the composed `ast` — the effective predicate, onto which the filters middleware may layer RLS / sharing narrowing;
- what a hook CAN reach is the caller's raw `options.where` (and `options.multi`);
- middleware only ever narrows, never widens, so treating the caller's predicate as the row set is an UPPER-BOUND approximation — the safe direction for a fail-closed guard (it may refuse too much, it can never miss).

The old sentence "A bulk write therefore hands hooks no queryable predicate" is exactly the one that was being misread, and is rewritten. The "scope ... at the CALLER" intent survives in the new paragraph, now with the reason it is true at the same time as "the composed `ast` is unreachable".

**3. There are three consumers, not two.** Besides plugin-auth's ban half (#5892) and delete half (#5941), objectql's own `isPredicateBulkWrite` (`hook-wrappers.ts`) reads `options.multi` off the same slot to tell a batch dispatch from a per-row one. Both the prose and the test header record this third one.

**4. `packages/objectql/src/hook-input-shape-contract.test.ts` — the positive pin** (4 cases: update/delete times by-id/multi). Each case asserts three things: reference identity `toBe(callerOptions)`, `options.where` deep-equal to the caller's predicate, and the existing `'ast' in input === false` restated in place, so the pair "composed unreachable / raw reachable" can only ever be read together. The pre-existing `'ast' in input === false` assertions are kept verbatim; the guarded surface does not shrink.

## Reverse verification (direction predicted first: RED — and it matched)

Counterfactual: replace the `before*` slot with a STRIPPED `DriverOptions` (the shape the old table row described), one line on each write path:

```
input: { id, options: (() => { const { where, multi, ...rest } = (opCtx.options ?? {}) as any;
                               return this.buildDriverOptions(object, opCtx.context, rest); })() },
```

Result — exactly the direction the card asks for:

```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  4 failed | 11 passed (15)
```

**The 4 new cases all go red; all 11 pre-existing cases stay green**, including section 2's `expect(seen[0]!.options).toBeDefined()` (a stripped bag is still `defined`). That gap is the measurement that makes this pin worth having: the suite as it stood could not tell the two shapes apart.

Run against the whole objectql package, the same counterfactual also reddens 2 further files (`hook-condition-bulk-previous.test.ts`, `hook-condition-fail-loud.test.ts`). That is consumer 3 above going blind once `multi` disappears — those tests do not assert this property directly, so they are not a substitute for the pin. The counterfactual was reverted with `git checkout --`; this PR's diff contains no `engine.ts` change.

## Generated artifacts

The contract table lives in a **JSDoc block**, not a `.describe()`, so the PM's assumption holds: after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:schema`, `git status --porcelain` was **empty** — zero regeneration under `packages/spec/json-schema/**` and `content/docs/references/**`, and zero drift in `authorable-surface.base.json`.

## Verification

- Gates enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and run one by one (43 `check:*`, all green): `nul-bytes`, `doc-authoring`, `adr-anchors`, `role-word`, `spec-parsed-alias`, `engine-double-contract`, `query-options-erasure`, `slot-lookup`, `error-code-casing`, `route-envelope`, `wildcard-fallthrough`, `meta-type-normalized`, `init-service-contract`, `durability-log-level`, `startup-registry-verdict`, `objectui-changeset`, `release-notes`, `release-body`, `node-version`, `workflow-status-functions`, `shard-attestation`, `published-files`, `resume-authority-declared`, `merge-driver`, `docs-audit-scope`, `org-identifier`, `authz-resolver`, `service-providers`, `quick-reference-counts`, `type-check-coverage`, `driver-conformance`, `stall-guard`, `i18n`, `i18n-coverage`, and spec-scoped `generated --reconcile-only`, `authorable-surface`, `spec-changes`, `upgrade-guide`, `skill-docs`, `docs`, `skill-refs`, `api-surface`, `exported-any`, `dual-source-exports`, `react-blocks`, `skill-frame-sync`, `skill-compatibility`.
  - `check:query-options-erasure` went **genuinely red** at first (test surface 263 to 264): my `engine.count('task', {} as any)` added an erasure site. Fixed the way the gate directs — type the options rather than raise the ratchet — by dropping the `as any` (`count(object, query?)` already infers the empty query). Back to 263, at the ceiling, none new.
  - `check:i18n` / `check:i18n-coverage` first reported an **environment prerequisite** (unbuilt CLI, `connector-mcp` with no dist), not a defect; both `EXIT=0` after `pnpm exec turbo run build`. Both gates warn that piping swallows their exit code, so they were read with `echo "EXIT=$?"`.
- `pnpm lint`: `EXIT=0`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` and `--filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: `EXIT=0`
- Tests, re-run after merging `origin/main`:

```
packages/spec test:  Test Files  338 passed (338)
packages/spec test:       Tests  8649 passed (8649)
packages/objectql test:  Test Files  140 passed (140)
packages/objectql test:       Tests  2325 passed (2325)
```

## In-flight overlap

I did not touch #6001's `positions` JSDoc stanza. Before pushing I ran `git merge origin/main` (no rebase, no force-push); at that point `git grep -c "services.sharing.canEdit" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` still returned `1`, so #6001 had not landed on main and there was nothing to clobber. This PR's diff on that file touches 0 `canEdit` lines. `hook.test.ts` (edited by PR #6243) is untouched; the pin went into `hook-input-shape-contract.test.ts`.

Changeset: `patch` (`@objectstack/spec` + `@objectstack/objectql`).
